subject: Tailwind Retail: mid-day runtime degradation & roadmap asks
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@tailwindretail.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-29T09:17:00-07:00
Subject: Mid-day runtime spike / throughput drop - urgent

Hi Soojin,

We're seeing a sharp degradation in Tailwind's checkout inference between 08:45 and 09:00 PDT this morning. Key symptoms: p99 generation latency jumped from ~210ms to ~1.1s, and overall throughput to our API pool dropped ~35%. The client logs show many longer sequences than usual and repeated retry traffic around 08:50.

I've attached a small set of perf graphs and a sample trace (perf-graphs-20280829.png, trace-sample-tailwind-0829.json). Can you triage and let us know:
- Any immediate mitigation we can expect (routing, throttles, temporary model fallback)?
- ETA for a mitigant and whether you can send a short customer-facing note explaining what happened and next steps?

This is impacting our checkout success rate so we need a short-term fix and a plan to avoid recurrence. Happy to join a bridge.

Thanks,
Elena Ruiz
Head of Platform
Tailwind Retail

From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@tailwindretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-29T09:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mid-day runtime spike / throughput drop - urgent

Elena — thanks for the quick heads up and the attachments. We're pulling people onto a bridge now.

Ben: can you and the runtime team take initial triage? Key asks:
- Confirm whether this is client-driven (sudden longer sequences / batching) vs runtime regression.
- If it's caching/kv thrash or kernel fallback, list the mitigations we can toggle (routing to dedicated pool, temporary throttling, disable batching on infra side).

Marissa: please draft a short customer note we can send to Tailwind by EOD with current impact, what we are doing, and next steps. Keep it clear about ETA for stabilization and whether we will offer credits.

Elena: we'll get back with a triage summary within 45 minutes and a proposed customer-facing note. If the bridge is helpful, propose 10:15 PDT and we'll confirm.

Attachments: confirmed received perf-graphs-20280829.png, trace-sample-tailwind-0829.json

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-29T09:58:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mid-day runtime spike / throughput drop - urgent

On Tue, Aug 29, 2028 at 09:17 AM Elena Ruiz <elena@tailwindretail.com> wrote:
> We're seeing a sharp degradation in Tailwind's checkout inference between 08:45 and 09:00 PDT this morning...

Quick triage notes from infra: initial hypothesis is a sudden client-side batching pattern change causing longer effective sequence lengths and a marked increase in KV cache eviction. Observations:
- GPU kernels flagged a fall-back to slower attention kernels for ~12% of requests in the window (we see this in the trace).
- KV cache hit-rate dropped from ~92% to ~57% for the affected shard group.
- Autoscaler did not immediately add capacity because per-instance CPU was high but overall GPU util stayed under alarm threshold.

Immediate mitigations we can enable (low risk):
1) Protective routing: divert Tailwind traffic to a dedicated capacity pool for 30-60m to avoid multitenant interference (requires Karthik/product sign-off).
2) On-the-fly kernel policy revert: rollback the last kernel selector change we rolled out to general pool (takes ~20m, risk: a small perf regression on other tenants).
3) Short-term client-side guidance: ask Tailwind to reduce max-batch and cap sequence lengths if possible — Marissa, can you surface a snippet for their engineers?

Next steps and ETA:
- I can enable protective routing in ~15m if product approves.
- If we roll back kernel selector, I expect p95/p99 to recover in 20–30m post-rollback and KV hit-rate to improve over an hour as caches warm.
- We'll capture a detailed postmortem and dataset of traces.

Karthik — flagging this because it touches routing policy, autoscaler thresholds, and whether we allow emergency pool carve-outs for large customers. If we want this to be a repeatable mitigation, we'll need a small product change to support scoped routing overrides for enterprise accounts.

Ben
Ben Carter
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@tailwindretail.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-30T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Tailwind interim update & customer note (proposed)

Hi Elena — following up with a short update and proposed customer-facing note.

Proposed note (short):
Hi Elena / Tailwind team,

Thanks again for flagging this. We identified a runtime interaction that amplified the impact of a change in your client batching pattern — this reduced our KV cache effectiveness and triggered a slower kernel path for a subset of requests.

What we did (interim):
- Diverted Tailwind traffic to a reserved capacity pool at 10:05 PDT to restore isolation and reduce tail latency.
- Rolled back the kernel selector change in the shared pool; we observed p99 reduce from ~1.1s to ~240ms within ~25 minutes.
- Continuing to monitor; our postmortem will include root cause and concrete recommendations for safe batching practices.

Next steps:
- Postmortem with timeline and remediation items by EOD tomorrow.
- Offer a service credit for the impacted window; we'll share specifics in the billing note.
- Work with your engineers on client-side batching caps and a recommended sequence-length policy.

If that looks good, we will send this formally and schedule a 30-minute bridge to walk through the postmortem tomorrow at 11:00 PDT.

Attachments: perf-graphs-20280829.png

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

— Soojin (quick ack): Please send the note and set the 11:00 bridge. Marissa, loop in Growth Billing for the credit note.
